Out of all the advice here, this is the best.

Easiest way to do it is when you are sitting around, watching TV or computering, or whatever it is you like to do, hold a milk jug full of water out, chest level and straight, for as long as you can. Offhand is important for rifles, Strong side is important for pistols.

Shrugs, straight dumbbell raises, and keeping doing what you’re doing. Save yourself ammo by using the weight of your rifle as resistance at home. Try switching arms because there is nothing wrong with offhand shooting for your non-dominant eye

Hold a 3lb weight in each hand, arms stretched out in front of you, and also do it straight out to the sides.

This is good for all your stabilizer muscles. Don't go crazy with the weight, though. Those muscles are small and if you damage them you're injured for a long time.
Push ups and Chin ups go a long long way and don't cost a gym membership

Dumbbell flies are a good exercise to work into a routine, as are pull-ups.

Another thing to consider is that when shooting, if you pull the rifle tight into your shoulder with your support hand this will limit the pain you end up feeling. Holding the loosely allows it to jerk back and slam into your shoulder, holding it tightly creates a slower and more gentle kind of push into the shoulder. This technique is a good argument in favor of using a handstop on your handguard to allow you to really crank the rifle back tightly.
